title: Introduce differential load prober and cross-zone variance absorber for canary evaluation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added a differential load prober that injects short micro-bursts across candidate and baseline routes plus a cross-zone variance absorber model that normalizes canary metrics by zone to reduce false positive regressions. Includes rollout guard that pauses cutovers when zonal variance exceeds threshold.
description:
Motivation: We observed spurious canary regressions when rolling models or scaling across AZs due to transient, zone-specific noise (maintenance, network fabric, NUMA imbalance) that was not indicative of model or runtime regressions. This PR implements a controlled differential load prober that issues paired micro-bursts to baseline and candidate paths with matched traffic shape, and a cross-zone variance absorber that learns per-zone latency/throughput baselines and adjusts canary statistics before evaluation. The goal is fewer false positives and more robust rollback decisions during multi-zone cutovers.

What this PR does (summary): 1) Adds a new prober implementation (differential_prober) used by perf-canary to schedule paired probes with precise timing jitter control and prioritized ordering so KV-cache state is comparable between probes. 2) Adds a cross-zone variance absorber that maintains lightweight per-zone summaries (EWMA of p50/p95/p99 and throughput) and applies a normalization transform to incoming probe metrics before they feed the canary evaluator. 3) Extends the canary evaluator to accept a normalized metrics stream and a new "variance_score" signal; if variance_score exceeds configured gate thresholds the rollout guard will automatically pause or throttle the cutover. 4) Adds observability: dashboards for per-zone residuals, a new metric canary.variance_score, and tagged traces for differential probe pairs. 5) Includes e2e tests and a simulation harness to exercise adversarial zone-noise scenarios.

Why this approach: Traditional single-probe comparisons are brittle when regional heterogeneity exists. By pairing probes and normalizing by short-term zone baselines we can better isolate candidate-induced regressions from infrastructure noise. The absorber model is intentionally simple (EWMA + variance shrinkage) to keep computation cheap and explainable.

Operational notes: Default gate is conservative (variance_score threshold 0.3) and disabled for single-zone deployments. Configuration is available via canary config (fields: differential_prober.enabled, absorber.window_seconds, absorber.threshold, absorber.min_samples). The rollout guard emits signals for automation: canary.pause_reason and canary.variance_score.

Backward compatibility: All changes are additive. Existing canary configs continue to work; the new prober and absorber are off by default.

Testing: Unit tests for scheduler and absorber math, integration tests against local perf-canary harness, and a staged canary run in perf-lab that reproduces a noisy-zone scenario.

Links: Linear ENG-2042 (reduce zone-driven false positives), SUP-4481 (customer incident investigating AZ noise), and internal runbook update (doc link omitted).
commits: feat(perf-canary): differential_prober implementation and scheduler hooks
feat(perf-canary): cross-zone variance absorber and normalization pipeline
chore(observability): add variance_score metric, dashboards and trace tags
test(perf-canary): e2e noisy-zone simulation and unit tests
fix(tuning): reduce probe jitter, tighten scheduler backoff after transient failures
review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice approach. A few questions: 1) How do we avoid probe-induced cache pollution affecting candidate/baseline symmetry? 2) Can the absorber drift under sustained asymmetric traffic? Please add explanatory comments and a small simulation that shows stability over 1 hour.

Author (Maya Chen): Reply: differential_prober pairs probes within <50ms and issues them in alternating order to balance cache warmup; probe payloads are cold by default and we added an optional cache-skip header for synthetic probes. The absorber includes a momentum clamp and min_samples to avoid drift; added an hour-long sim and results in tests/test_zone_absorber.py.
Sofia Martinez: Lint and type issues in zone_absorber.py, also prefer explicit floats for EWMA alpha. Also can we expose a debug endpoint to snapshot per-zone state?
Author (Maya Chen): Addressed: fixed typing, made alpha explicit and added a debug snapshots endpoint behind admin feature flag (observability/dashboards references that endpoint).
Rahul Gupta: CI e2e failed on first run (timing-flaky). Can we add retry/backoff to the harness? Also confirm negligible CPU overhead for absorber on 1000 zones.
Author (Maya Chen): Added exponential retry in perf-lab harness; measured absorber at ~0.6% CPU on synthetic 1000-zone run (reported in PR comment and perf-lab job logs).
notes_on_rollback_guard: Rollout guard behavior: when variance_score > absorber.threshold, canary evaluator will emit a 'pause' signal. The operator can configure automatic rollback or manual inspection. Guard has a cooldown window to avoid thrashing; default cooldown 300s. The absorber updates persist to local state store and are checkpointed to S3 for Private customers.
